key_insight: The temperature-driven band-gap bowing in FA–MA lead iodide perovskites is mainly caused by an anomalous electron-phonon coupling triggered by low-frequency FA cation rattling modes, with thermal expansion playing a secondary role.
engineering_relevance: Understanding this mixed-cation, temperature-dependent gap mechanism helps engineers better predict and tune perovskite optoelectronic performance across operating conditions.
method: Temperature-dependent photoluminescence on FAxMA1−xPbI3 single crystals (x = 0 to 1)
Pressure-dependent photoluminescence to separate thermal expansion from electron-phonon effects
Composition and phase analysis across orthorhombic and (pseudo)tetragonal low-temperature regimes
evidence_signal: The study uses a series of mixed-cation single crystals and combined temperature/pressure measurements to attribute the observed gap bowing to competing thermal expansion and electron-phonon coupling effects, with the latter dominant.
watch_item: The proposed mechanism is inferred for low-temperature phases and may depend on stripe-domain formation and phase structure, so direct transfer to operating-device conditions should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Origin of the Temperature-Induced Gap Bowing of Formamidinium-Methylammonium Lead Iodide Perovskites: Role of Cationic Rattlers
